chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The shroud is from the entirety of the wealth.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْكَفَنُ: The shroud or burial cloth used for the deceased.

ai.seo_question: How is the cost of the shroud paid from the deceased's estate according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi establishes the priority of burial expenses (kafan) over debts and bequests, reflecting the principle that honoring the deceased's body is a fundamental right of the soul. Scholars note that this ruling underscores the dignity of the dead, ensuring that the physical preparation for the afterlife is funded directly from the estate's assets before any financial obligations are settled.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The shroud is from the entirety of the wealth (legacy)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ‘ Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The shroud is paid for from the whole of the legacy.”’
